figures.cap: building, window and car with 40 degree angle of depression

parts.latex:
The angle of depression from a window to a car on the ground is $40^\circ$.

The car is 50 metres from the base of the building.

\exfigure{719_q10_1}

How high above the ground is the base of the window, correct to the nearest metre?

solutions.latex:
The horizontal dashed line is parallel to the ground, so the angle of elevation from the car to the window is also $40^\circ$ (alternate angles).

In the right-angled triangle, the side opposite $40^\circ$ is the height $h$ and the adjacent side is $50$ m, so use $\tan$.
$$\begin{aligned} \tan 40^\circ &= \dfrac{h}{50} \\ h &= 50\tan 40^\circ \\ &\approx 41.95 \\ &\approx 42 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is option C.

719_q10_1.notes: Brick wall with window, dashed horizontal, sight line to the car, 40° arc with a filled arrowhead, a right-angle mark, the 50 m dimension line (dashed, filled heads, end bars, gap left for the label), NOT TO SCALE and Car. Positions measured from the crop. What is left in the overlay is the spacing of the brick courses in the lower wall and the simplified car outline; all lines, the arc and labels sit in place. Rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 6a, 11. 6162.stem:
Robert walks 5.59 km from his house to the shop on a bearing of 063°. He then turns on a bearing of 124° to walk to the post office, where he is 13.34 km from home.

\exfigure{719_q22_1}

figures.cap: bearing diagram House, Shop, Post office
solution sketch: bearing diagram annotated with angles x, y, 56 degrees, 27 degrees

parts.latex: Find the true bearing of Robert’s house from the post office.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{719_q22_s1}

Let $x$ and $y$ be the angles at $S$ on either side of the north line through $S$, so $\angle HSP = x + y$.
$$y = 180 - 124 = 56^\circ$$
$$x = 63^\circ \quad (\text{alternate angles, parallel north lines})$$
$$\begin{aligned} \angle HSP &= 56 + 63 \\ &= 119^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none). Source drawing kept.

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule in triangle $HSP$, with $Z = \angle HPS$:
$$\dfrac{\sin Z}{5.59} = \dfrac{\sin 119^\circ}{13.34}$$
$$\begin{aligned} Z &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5.59 \sin 119^\circ}{13.34}\right) \\ &= 21.49\ldots \\ &\approx 21^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing of } H \text{ from } P &= 360 - (56 + 21) \\ &= 283^\circ\text{T} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the sine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

Small differences in label position remain (scan font vs house font). Rules 3, 4, 11, 22.

figures.cap: triangle ABC with sides AC=6, AB=7, BC=8

parts.latex:
What is the smallest angle in the following triangle?

\exfigure{1247_q8_1}

solutions.latex:
In a triangle, the smallest angle is opposite the shortest side.

The sides are $AB=7$, $BC=8$ and $AC=6$, so the shortest side is $AC=6$.

The angle opposite $AC$ is $\angle B$.
$$\therefore\ \text{the smallest angle is } B$$

meta.generated_note: MCQ working written for key B.

solution sketch: radial survey diagram annotated with angle 138° and side AB

parts.latex: Calculate the distance of $AB$ to the nearest 2 decimal places.

criteria: Uses the correct angle ($138^\circ$), or equivalent merit
Applies the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule,
$$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{43}=\dfrac{\sin 138^\circ}{74.72}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \theta &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{43\sin 138^\circ}{74.72}\right) \\ &= 22^\circ 39' \end{aligned}$$
Using co-interior angles, the bearing is
$$120^\circ-22^\circ39'\approx 097^\circ\text{T}$$
criteria: Correct answer in true bearing form
Uses co-interior angles, or equivalent merit
Applies the sine rule, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: triangle of towns T1, T2, T3 with north line
solution sketch: bearing diagram annotated with angles 150, 30, 20 and theta

parts.latex:
The distance between towns $T_1$ and $T_2$ is 35 km and the distance between towns $T_2$ and $T_3$ is 40 km. as shown in the diagram below.

\exfigure{717_q41_1}

The bearings of town $T_3$ from town $T_1$ is $150^\circ$ and the bearing of town $T_2$ from town $T_3$ is $020^\circ$.

What is the bearing of town $T_2$ from town $T_1$ to the nearest degree?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{717_q41_s1}

Using the sine rule in $\triangle T_1T_2T_3$, with $\theta=\angle T_2T_1T_3$:
$$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{40}=\dfrac{\sin 50^\circ}{35}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \sin\theta &= \dfrac{40\sin 50^\circ}{35} \\ \theta &\approx 61^\circ \end{aligned}$$
The bearing of $T_2$ from $T_1$ is
$$150^\circ-61^\circ=089^\circ$$
criteria: Sets up the sine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Kept source \exfigure. Rubric written by us.
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

figures.cap: solution sketch: diagram of Lachlan, eagle and nest

parts.latex:
Lachlan is at a lookout. He looks up and sees a white-bellied sea eagle.

The distance from Lachlan to the eagle is 153 metres and it is at an angle of elevation of $63^\circ$.

Lachlan looks down and sees the eagle's nest. The distance from Lachlan to the nest is 87 metres and it is at an angle of depression of $27^\circ$.

Calculate the distance of the eagle from its nest. Answer correct to the nearest metre.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{1266_q22_s1}

The angles at Lachlan add to a right angle.
$$63^\circ + 27^\circ = 90^\circ$$
Hence the triangle is right angled, and by Pythagoras' theorem
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Distance} &= \sqrt{153^2 + 87^2} \\ &\approx 176 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds that the triangle is right angled, or equivalent merit
Sketches a diagram correctly showing all information, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: pole PQ and building RT with sight lines from P

parts.latex: Mark the given information on the diagram.
Use this information to calculate the size of $\angle PRT$.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{825_q30_s1}

The angles of depression are measured from the horizontal line through $P$ (parallel to $QT$). Mark $29^\circ$ between this horizontal and $PR$, and $65^\circ$ between this horizontal and $PT$.

In $\triangle PRT$, the angle at $P$ is the difference between the two angles of depression.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle RPT &= 65^\circ - 29^\circ \\ &= 36^\circ \end{aligned}$$
The angle of depression of $T$ equals $\angle PTQ$ (alternate angles, horizontal through $P$ parallel to $QT$), so $\angle PTQ = 65^\circ$. Since $RT$ is vertical, $\angle RTQ = 90^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle PTR &= 90^\circ - 65^\circ \\ &= 25^\circ \end{aligned}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle PRT$:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle PRT &= 180^\circ - 36^\circ - 25^\circ \\ &= 119^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \angle PRT = 119^\circ$$

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

7089.stem: The angle of elevation from a boat ($B$) to the top of a lighthouse ($L$) is $19^\circ$ and the angle of elevation from a ship ($S$) to the top of a lighthouse is $10^\circ$. The distance between the boat and the ship is 119 m.

figures.cap: lighthouse with two lines of sight to the water and a horizontal dashed line
solution sketch: labelled lighthouse diagram with angles and lengths

parts.latex:
Label the diagram below using all the above information

\exfigure{713_q14_1}
Calculate the height of the lighthouse, correct to the nearest metre.

solutions.latex:
Label $L$ (top of lighthouse), $G$ (base), $X$ (on the horizontal through $L$), $B$ and $S$.

The labels are $\angle LBG=19^\circ$, $\angle LSB=10^\circ$ and $BS=119$ m.

The alternate angle is $\angle XLS=10^\circ$.

\exfigure{713_q14_s1}
criteria: Labels some of the given information correctly, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
In the diagram, $\angle LBS$ is supplementary to the $19^\circ$ angle of elevation at $B$.

$$\begin{aligned} \angle LBS &= 180^\circ-19^\circ \\ &= 161^\circ \end{aligned}$$

(supplementary angles)

$$\angle XLS=\angle LSB=10^\circ$$

(alternate angles, parallel lines)

Using the angle sum of triangle $LBS$:

$$\begin{aligned} \angle SLB &= 180^\circ-(161^\circ+10^\circ) \\ &= 9^\circ \end{aligned}$$

Applying the sine rule in triangle $LBS$:

$$\dfrac{LB}{\sin 10^\circ}=\dfrac{BS}{\sin 9^\circ}$$

$$\begin{aligned} LB &= \dfrac{119\sin 10^\circ}{\sin 9^\circ} \\ &\approx 132.09 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

In the right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $LB$ and vertical side $LG$:

$$\sin 19^\circ=\dfrac{LG}{132.09}$$

$$\begin{aligned} LG &= 132.09\sin 19^\circ \\ &\approx 43 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ \text{the height of the lighthouse is } 43 \text{ m}$$

meta.format_note: Source had no rubric; rubric written by us in top-down form. G taken as the foot of the lighthouse (source uses LG).
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

7367.stem:
The diagram shows a vertical pole $PQ$ and a building $RT$, both standing on level ground.

From the top of the pole the angle of depression of the top of the building is $32^\circ$ and of the base of the building is $68^\circ$.

On a direct line of sight from the top of the pole to the base of the building, the distance is 55 m.

\exfigure{235_q31_1}

figures.cap: pole PQ and building RT on level ground with sight lines from P

parts.latex: Mark the given information on the diagram and explain why $\angle PRT$ is $122^\circ$.
Use the Sine rule to calculate the height of the building $RT$ correct to the nearest metre.
How much taller is pole, than the building?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{235_q31_s1}

The horizontal through $P$ is parallel to $QT$. So, with alternate angles between parallel lines:

$\angle PTQ = 68^\circ$ (angle of depression of $T$)

$\angle RPT = 68^\circ - 32^\circ = 36^\circ$ (the line of sight to $R$ is $32^\circ$ below the horizontal, the line to $T$ is $68^\circ$ below it)

The building is vertical, so $\angle RTQ = 90^\circ$, giving
$$\angle PTR = 90^\circ - 68^\circ = 22^\circ$$
Angle sum in triangle $PRT$:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle PRT &= 180^\circ - 36^\circ - 22^\circ \\ &= 122^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \angle PRT = 122^\circ$$
criteria: Marks the given information on the diagram and finds $\angle RPT = 36^\circ$ and $\angle PTR = 22^\circ$, or equivalent merit
Finds one of $\angle RPT$ or $\angle PTR$, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: Written by us; no source solution.

solutions.latex:
In triangle $PRT$: $\angle RPT = 36^\circ$, $\angle PRT = 122^\circ$ and $PT = 55$ (opposite $\angle PRT$). Using the sine rule:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{RT}{\sin 36^\circ} &= \dfrac{55}{\sin 122^\circ} \\ RT &= \dfrac{55\sin 36^\circ}{\sin 122^\circ} \\ &\approx 38.1 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ RT \approx 38 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the sine rule, or equivalent merit
Identifies the correct angle and side pair, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: Written by us; no source solution.
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
In the right-angled triangle $PQT$, $PT = 55$ is the hypotenuse and $\angle PTQ = 68^\circ$, so $PQ$ is opposite the angle:
$$\begin{aligned} PQ &= 55\sin 68^\circ \\ &\approx 50.99 \\ &\approx 51 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
The difference in height is
$$51 - 38 = 13 \text{ m}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the pole is } 13 \text{ m taller than the building}$$
criteria: Finds the height of the pole, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: Written by us; no source solution.
meta.final: the pole is $13$ m taller than the building
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)
